messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: High rate-limit rejections (429) observed for org=OrchidWorks since 1758901200. Symptom: spike in generation requests, errors surfaced in customer's app. Paging @jordan_oncall and @jonas_sre. See quick metrics: https://internal.redwood/telemetry/orgs/OrchidWorks/overview

jordan_oncall: On it. Acknowledge. Can someone paste the customer-reported error?

maria_support: OrchidWorks engineer sent this at 15:07 UTC: "We're seeing many 429s when sending batches, started ~15:00. Traffic pattern looks like a replay job. Impact: user-facing failures on prod." They've paused upstream retries.

jonas_sre: Looking at infra panels now — per-org limiter is triggering at 120 req/s, token bucket exhausted. Recent deploys didn't touch limiter config. QPS from OrchidWorks jumped to ~900 rps sustained for 6m.

jordan_oncall: So it's a customer-induced spike. Immediate mitigation options: 1) increase per-org rate cap temporarily, 2) enable org-scoped burst smoothing, 3) ask customer to throttle. Which one lowest risk?

dina_englead: If they need immediate relief, do a surgical per-org cap bump with a short TTL (10–15m) and tight guardrails. We must record the change and auto-roll back. Approve if SRE comfortable.

jonas_sre: I can perform a targeted cap bump via admin API. Runbook: 
```
POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/orgs/OrchidWorks/limits
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer {{SRE_API_TOKEN}}

{ "per_second": 240, "ttl_seconds": 900, "reason": "emergency-surge-orchidworks-1758901234" }
```
Will monitor for errors and latency.

jordan_oncall: :thumbsup: Please comment when started. Maria, can you confirm customer consent? Carla, CSM loop?

carla_csm: I just DM'd their lead — they asked for immediate relief and will throttle their replay if we can buy 15m. They approve the narrow bump.

jonas_sre: Executing now. 
```
> curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/orgs/OrchidWorks/limits \
>  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
>  -d '{"per_second":240,"ttl_seconds":900,"reason":"emergency-surge-orchidworks-1758901234"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","applied_until":1758902134}
```
jonas_sre: Applied. Monitor links: infra alert -> https://internal.redwood/alerts/17589, org traffic -> https://internal.redwood/telemetry/orgs/OrchidWorks/overview, limiter logs -> https://logs.redwood/service/ratelimiter?org=OrchidWorks

hawk_monitor: Auto-checks: token drop rate decreased from 14%->1.2% in 60s. Error rate (429) dropping. No other orgs affected.

jordan_oncall: Customer errors dropping? Maria?

maria_support: OrchidWorks confirms errors fell to near-zero within 90s. They're resuming normal processing and will backfill slowly.

dina_englead: Good. Keep the TTL; set a manual rollback in 10m if stable. Also record for postmortem.

jonas_sre: Setting a rollback job for 10m from now. Also adding a short-lived alert to catch re-trigger: 
```
POST /jobs/schedule {"job":"revert-org-limit","org":"OrchidWorks","run_at":1758901834}
```

jordan_oncall: Noted. Any secondary mitigations needed (circuit-breakers, cached prefixes)?

jonas_sre: No, not necessary now. We're keeping an eye on system wide batching. No cascading latencies seen.

hawk_monitor: FYI: CPU on a couple serving nodes rose 10% during the spike but within SLO. No pod restarts.

carla_csm: I'll draft a customer-facing note: explain we applied a temporary cap increase and recommended they throttle replays; ask for their planned remediation.

jonas_sre: 10 minutes elapsed — reverting per-runbook. Reverting now. 
```
> curl -X POST https://admin.internal.redwood/api/orgs/OrchidWorks/limits/revert \
>  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
>  -d '{"reason":"revert-after-stable","initiator":"jonas_sre","thread":"1758901234"}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","current_per_second":120}
```

hawk_monitor: Post-revert checks: 429s remain low (0.8%). Orchids confirm they're continuing to pace.

jordan_oncall: Great. Close the page once we have a short notes summary for incident log. Any follow-ups?

dina_englead: Follow-ups: 1) capture the traffic spike patterns in the org's evals, 2) consider a proactive org-guard for replay-like burst profiles, 3) review admin API authorization audit for emergency changes. Assign owners.

carla_csm: I'll own customer comms and collect their replay schedule.

jonas_sre: I'll file an infra ticket to add a temporary guard and link telemetry graphs.

maria_support: Adding incident to incident-tracker and tagging as "surgical-rate-bump". Quick summary for logs: "Applied 2x per-second cap to OrchidWorks for 15m to mitigate replay-induced 429 surge; reverted after stabilization; customer to throttle replays."

jordan_oncall: Closing thread in 30m if no regressions. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
